text.p: Italian bonds and futures outperformed other European debt markets, ending quietly firmer but off session highs in what traders said was a technical rebound helped by the firmer lira.
But the mood was cautious and the underlying tone remains bearish with the market, made up of mainly domestic players on Wednesday, closely watching the U.S. and Treasuries.

"There's some renewed hope in Italy for its own sake, but until we see for example good April CPI data there are no real internal factors to move the market, we'll just follow the U.S.," one trader said.

Operators were awaiting U.S. non-farm payroll data Friday. U.S. debt futures were off lows but weak, showing little reaction to February factory orders, up 0.8 pct against a forecast 0.9 pct rise and against January's 2.5 pct increase.
The June Btp future was stuck around 124.50 for most of the afternoon, unable to overcome resistance at 124.75.
"On the charts the outlook is bearish. June could rise above 124.75 but it could likely breach 124.20 which isn't a strong support level, so best avoid long positions," one trader said.
The lira extended gains against the mark in thin trade with dealers talking of a technical move independent of the dollar.

On the domestic Italian front, "I don't think we'll see massive foreign buying until around May when local elections are out of the way, the government's future should be clearer and we have some details about reform of the welfare state," one trader said.
For the moment, "there's the Dow Jones to watch," while further on "if there's a hike in rates in Japan then all the markets will be affected," another said.
